lines.text: Hi there, explorer! I'm Astro, and I'll be your guide on a trip through our solar system.
Our solar system has one star, the Sun, with eight planets, dwarf planets like Pluto, and many moons circling around it.
Let's start with Mars, the Red Planet. It gets its colour from rusty red dust that covers the ground.
The air on Mars is very thin, so you would need a spacesuit there. It is also home to Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano we know of.
No person has visited Mars yet, but robots have! Rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance drive across it and send home pictures.
Now look closer to home. The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, and it is covered in craters left by ancient space rocks.
In 1969, Apollo 11 astronauts became the first people to walk on the Moon. Six Apollo missions landed there in all.
Gravity on the Moon is only about one-sixth of Earth's, so astronauts could bounce along in giant, slow leaps.
Ready to see for yourself? Pick Mars or the Moon, and let's go exploring together!
